text: BIS Care application BIS provides the official BIS Care application as a consumer-facing service.
Verify HUID BIS hallmarking FAQ provides consumer guidance on HUID verification through BIS Care.
Hallmarking consumer protection BIS publishes consumer protection guidance for hallmarking, including verification and complaint-related information.
BIS consumer affairs BIS maintains a consumer affairs section covering consumer-oriented standards and services.
BIS consumer grievance BIS provides a consumer grievance channel as part of its consumer-facing services.
BIS Care languages BIS says the BIS Care app supports 12 languages, including regional languages, Hindi and English.
Verify licence feature BIS Care provides a Verify Licence Details feature for checking authenticity of products bearing the relevant mark.
Verify HUID feature BIS Care provides Verify HUID for hallmarked jewellery.
Know Your Standards feature BIS Care links consumers to information on Indian Standards, licences against them and laboratories for the product.
BIS locations feature BIS Care provides locations of BIS laboratories and offices.
Certification guides BIS Care provides step-by-step guidance for Simplified, CRS and Normal Procedure licences.
Consumer jewellery testing Consumers can get jewellery or samples tested at BIS-recognized Assaying & Hallmarking Centres on a chargeable basis.
Assay report The A&H Centre is required to issue an assay report containing proper identification as marked on the article.

How much does BIS product testing cost? BIS testing cost is not one universal fixed amount. The applicable laboratory testing charge depends on the product, applicable Indian Standard, laboratory, test scope and the tests required. The RAG must retrieve the applicable laboratory scope and current fee information rather than quote a generic amount.

Where can I find the current testing charge for a BIS test? Current testing charges should be taken from the applicable BIS LIMS laboratory scope/fee information or the authoritative BIS document for that test. The answer should identify the laboratory and applicable standard/test before quoting an amount.

Does every BIS-recognized laboratory charge the same testing fee? Do not assume that all BIS-recognized laboratories charge the same amount. Fees must be checked against the applicable laboratory and its current published scope/charge information.

Can I know the testing cost before sending my product to a laboratory? Yes, where the laboratory publishes applicable charges, the current BIS LIMS scope/fee information can be used to identify the relevant test and charge. The exact amount should be quoted only when supported by current authoritative laboratory data.

What information is needed to estimate laboratory testing cost? At minimum, identify the product, applicable Indian Standard, required test or test group, and the laboratory whose scope is being considered. Different tests and laboratories can have different charges.

Can the BIS assistant give me a testing fee for my product? It should give a testing fee only when the current authoritative laboratory record supports the amount and identifies the relevant standard/test. If the current fee is unavailable, it should say that the fee could not be verified instead of estimating it.

What is the difference between BIS product certification fees and laboratory testing charges? They are different categories of cost. A laboratory may charge for testing, while BIS certification involves its own applicable certification, application, inspection or other prescribed charges. The assistant should retrieve each applicable fee separately rather than combine them into one unsupported total.

Will testing cost be the same for every product under BIS certification? No universal amount should be assumed. Testing requirements and applicable charges depend on the product, applicable Indian Standard, tests and laboratory scope.

How do I find a laboratory that can test my product? Identify the applicable Indian Standard and then use the BIS LIMS laboratory directory and scope records to find laboratories whose published scope includes the required standard/test.

Can I use any laboratory for BIS-required testing? Not automatically. The applicable certification scheme or requirement determines what laboratory status is acceptable. The assistant should verify the relevant BIS requirement and the laboratory's current recognized/empanelled status and scope.

What if the laboratory fee is not available online? The assistant should state that the current fee could not be verified from the authoritative source. It should not infer a fee from another laboratory or from an old record.

Can the same test have different charges at different laboratories? A generic single charge should not be assumed. Current laboratory-specific fee information should be checked for the required test and standard.

How much does jewellery purity testing cost under BIS hallmarking? The BIS Hallmarking FAQ states that a consumer can get jewellery tested at a recognized Assaying & Hallmarking Centre and identifies a ₹200 fire-assay testing charge in the stated context. The assistant should cite the current BIS FAQ when giving this amount.

Can a consumer test jewellery at a BIS-recognized Assaying & Hallmarking Centre? Yes. BIS consumer guidance states that consumers can get jewellery tested at a BIS-recognized Assaying & Hallmarking Centre, subject to the applicable procedure and report requirements.

What should I ask a laboratory before sending a sample? Confirm the applicable Indian Standard/test, whether the laboratory's current BIS scope covers the required test, the current testing charge, sample requirements, turnaround information where published, and the required report format.

Why should the BIS assistant avoid giving an estimated laboratory fee? A guessed fee can be wrong because laboratory charges are tied to the specific test, standard, laboratory and current fee schedule. The assistant should provide only an amount supported by current authoritative evidence.

What if I only know my product name but not the Indian Standard? First identify the applicable Indian Standard from authoritative BIS product/standard information. Laboratory selection and testing cost should be determined only after the relevant standard and test requirements are established.

Does a laboratory's published scope prove that every test is currently available? The assistant should use the current BIS LIMS scope and status information and should not infer availability beyond what the authoritative record states.

Can I ask for a complete testing-cost estimate? Yes, but the estimate must be assembled from verified applicable costs. The assistant should distinguish laboratory testing charges from BIS certification fees and clearly identify any cost that could not be verified.

What should the assistant say if there is no current fee for my required test? It should explicitly state that the current fee could not be verified from the authoritative BIS source and provide the relevant laboratory or source page for further verification, rather than inventing a number.

 1. INTRODUCTION  
 
1.1 Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), the National Standards Body (NSB) of India was 
established under the BIS Act, 1986 and came into existence on 1 April 1987 assuming the 
functions of the erstwhile Indian Standards Institution (ISI). The ISI came into being  on 6 January 
1947. Subsequently , the BIS Act, 2016 came into force on 12 October 2017 superseding BIS Act 
1986  and provided for BIS to be the N ational Standards Body, responsible for the harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, conform ity assessment and quality assurance of

Hallmarking overview BIS provides the statutory hallmarking framework for precious-metal articles, including hallmarking centres, jeweller registration, consumer protection and related guidance.

Hallmark Unique Identification (HUID) BIS hallmarking guidance describes HUID as a six-digit alphanumeric identifier associated with hallmarked jewellery. Consumers can use BIS Care to verify HUID information.

Gold hallmarking standard The supplied report identifies IS 1417 as the standard reference for gold and gold alloys. This record is retained as a research lead and must be reconciled against the authoritative current standard catalogue before being treated as normative.

Silver hallmarking standard The supplied report identifies IS 2112 as the standard reference for silver hallmarking. This record is retained as a research lead and must be reconciled against the authoritative current standard catalogue before normative use.

Hallmarking regulations The supplied report references the BIS (Hallmarking) Regulations, 2018 for hallmarking regulatory requirements and fee schedules. Current legal text should be sourced and versioned from BIS before normative use.

Hallmarking source map Authoritative BIS hallmarking information is distributed across hallmarking overview, FAQs, jeweller guidance, A&H Centre information, consumer protection pages and official lists/directories.

Mandatory hallmarking rollout claims The supplied report describes phased mandatory hallmarking rollout and district coverage. These historical claims should be validated against the exact orders/gazette instruments before being promoted to normative knowledge.

AHC/OSC operational claims The supplied report contains detailed AHC and Offsite Centre operational limits, timelines and fees. These are retained as research leads only until the corresponding current BIS orders/guidelines are individually acquired and reconciled.
Definition of hallmarking Hallmarking is the accurate determination and official recording of the proportionate content of precious metal in precious-metal articles.
Precious metals currently covered BIS states that gold and silver are the two precious metals currently brought under the hallmarking framework in India.
IS 1417:2016 BIS identifies IS 1417:2016 as the standard for gold and gold alloys, jewellery/artefacts, fineness and marking specification.
IS 2112:2014 BIS identifies IS 2112:2014 as the standard for silver and silver alloys, jewellery/artefacts, fineness and marking specification.
IS 15820:2009 BIS identifies IS 15820:2009 as the general requirements standard for establishment and operation of Assaying and Hallmarking Centres.
IS 1418:2009 BIS identifies IS 1418:2009 as the method for determination of gold in bullion, alloys and jewellery/artefacts by cupellation (fire assay).
IS 2113:2014 BIS identifies IS 2113:2014 as an assaying method standard for silver and silver alloys.
HUID format HUID is a six-digit alphanumeric number, unique for each hallmarked item and traceable.
Current three-mark hallmark Since introduction of HUID on 1 July 2021, BIS states that hallmark consists of BIS logo, purity in caratage/fineness and six-digit alphanumeric HUID.
Hallmarking charges BIS states hallmarking charges are paid per article irrespective of article weight.
Invoice requirements BIS consumer FAQ states the bill/invoice should include article description, net precious-metal weight, purity in carat/fineness and hallmarking charges.
Pairs of jewellery BIS consumer FAQ states each article in a pair should have hallmarking and fineness details should be checked on each article.
Detachable jewellery parts BIS consumer FAQ states each detachable part of jewellery should have a hallmark.

Retail display requirements BIS guidance states registered/certified jewellers should display BIS signage, certificate, hallmark information and a minimum 10X magnifying glass for customer inspection.
Old jewellery FAQ BIS's common-consumer FAQ states that old jewellery cannot be hallmarked under the cited FAQ response.
Hallmark fee scope BIS consumer FAQ states hallmarking charges do not include making charges or wastage charges.
Mandatory hallmarking order page The BIS mandatory hallmarking page provides the order and a sequence of amendments spanning 2020 through 2026.
Current amendment listing The official BIS page currently lists amendments dated 2 March 2026, 28 April 2026 and 3 August 2026.
District coverage resources The official mandatory hallmarking page links phase-wise district coverage resources and additional district lists.
AHC recognition basis BIS states recognition of Assaying and Hallmarking Centres is based on IS 15820:2009 and requires an application, Quality Manual, applicable fees and prescribed guidelines.
AHC resource set BIS provides AHC guidelines, a list of hallmarking centres, a generic quality manual and a list of cancelled/expired/suspended AHCs.
Offsite centre guidance BIS publishes separate Guidelines on Offsite Centres of AHCs, so OSC requirements should be retrieved as a distinct evidence class.
Refinery gold-only scope BIS states the hallmarking scheme for bullion/coin by refineries/mints is presently available for gold.
Refinery application channel BIS states refinery/mint applications are accepted online through Manakonline, including payments.
Refinery applicant eligibility BIS states manufacturers engaged in refining by aqua-regia/electrolytic process or minting precious metals may apply under the Hallmarking Regulations framework.
Refinery prerequisites BIS lists in-house manufacturing and testing capability and laboratory accreditation by NABL or LBMA as prerequisites.
Refinery licence scope BIS states refinery/mint licence scope covers gold bullion or gold coin, fineness 999 or 995, and declared design/weight, with no negative tolerance on declared weight.
Refinery licence validity BIS states refinery/mint licence is initially valid for one year and may be renewed for a maximum period of two years.

Refinery marking fee BIS states minimum annual marking fee is ₹48,000 for large-scale gold refineries and ₹38,400 for MSME units, with production-based marking fee of ₹50 per unit where one unit equals 1 kg.

Laboratory scope warning BIS LIMS states that scope information displayed in the database is submitted by the laboratory and is subject to verification by BIS; information outside granted recognition scope is the laboratory's responsibility. The assistant should therefore check scope before recommending a laboratory for a specific standard/test.

Product certification licence process BIS states that the application process begins by identifying the applicable Indian Standard, followed by assessment of manufacturing infrastructure, process controls, quality control and testing capabilities; applications and payments are online through Manakonline.

Compulsory BIS certification BIS product certification FAQ states that products are brought under compulsory certification by the Central Government under the BIS Act, 2016 or other Acts; products in the official compulsory-certification list require a BIS licence.

Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme BIS FMCS guidance requires an applicant to complete the prescribed application, nominate an Authorized Indian Representative and submit required documentation and fees; online submission through Manakonline is required from 1 June 2026.

CRS registered manufacturer directory The official CRS registry exposes registered manufacturer information including registration number, manufacturer, address, product, IS number, grant date, status, validity, scope and brand.
CRS registration workflow The CRS portal provides the registration workflow for covered electronics and IT products, including test report submission and online registration processes.
Jeweller registration BIS hallmarking information provides the official route for jeweller registration and related hallmarking requirements.

Scheme-I product certification BIS product certification overview provides Scheme-I certification process resources, including grant, suspension/revocation, scope change, renewal, retesting and operation guidance.
Product Manuals BIS product certification provides Product Manuals as product-specific technical guidance.
SIT resource BIS product certification provides Schemes of Inspection and Testing as product-specific information.
Grouping Guidelines BIS product certification provides grouping guidelines for product certification.
Testing facility search BIS product certification provides an IS-wise search facility for laboratories.
Product manual contents BIS says Product Manuals include sampling guidelines, test equipment lists, SIT and scope description.

New product with no product manual BIS FAQ states a product may still be eligible for a Scheme-I licence when product-specific guidance or marking fee is not defined, subject to the applicable regulations.
FMCS application FMCS requires the prescribed application and documentation.
Authorized Indian Representative FMCS requires nomination of an Authorized Indian Representative using the prescribed form.
FMCS online-only change BIS states FMCS hard-copy applications were accepted only up to 31 May 2026 and online submission is required from 1 June 2026.
CRS legal scheme CRS is operated under Scheme-II of the BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018.
CRS manufacturer registration BIS registers manufacturers under CRS so qualifying articles may declare conformity and use the notified Standard Mark.
CRS product catalogue The official CRS site publishes products covered under CRS together with Indian Standard numbers and implementation dates.

Empanelled laboratory directory fields BIS LIMS publishes an official empanelled-laboratory directory. Individual scope should be taken from the official scope facility where available rather than inferred from the laboratory name.
Gold refinery scheme scope BIS refinery guidance covers gold bullion/coin licensing and related fineness, testing, marking and accreditation requirements.
BIS Care language support BIS describes BIS Care as an official consumer application supporting multiple Indian languages and verification/service features.
Assaying and Hallmarking Centre guidance BIS publishes guidelines, quality documentation and official centre resources for Assaying and Hallmarking Centres.
HUID definition and traceability BIS states that HUID is a six-digit alphanumeric unique identification number for a hallmarked item and supports traceability through BIS systems.

Hallmarking FAQ: applicable precious metals and standards BIS Hallmarking FAQ identifies gold and silver as covered precious metals and references IS 1417 for gold/gold alloys and IS 2112 for silver/silver alloys, along with assaying and AHC standards.
BIS recognized laboratory directory BIS LIMS publishes the recognized laboratory directory. The current LIMS home page reports 431 recognized laboratories.
BIS FAQ index BIS maintains an official FAQ section containing answers and guidance for BIS services and programmes.

Consumer jewellery testing at AHC BIS consumer protection guidance states that consumers can have jewellery tested at a BIS-recognized Assaying and Hallmarking Centre on a chargeable basis and receive an assay report.
CRS Scheme II scope BIS CRS describes the Compulsory Registration Scheme as Scheme II, under which covered products are subject to registration requirements.

BIS Care official app capabilities BIS states that BIS Care provides services including Verify Licence Details, Verify HUID, Know Your Standards, laboratory and office locations, and step-by-step guidance for certification schemes.
BIS laboratory services BIS provides IS-wise laboratory information and recognized laboratory resources through its laboratory services and LIMS systems.
Product certification Scheme I BIS product certification resources cover Scheme I processes including grant, suspension, revocation, scope changes, renewal, retesting and operation.
Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme BIS provides the current FMCS application process and related requirements for foreign manufacturers.
Hallmarking charge basis BIS Hallmarking FAQ states that hallmarking charges are levied per article rather than by weight.
BIS consumer grievance service BIS provides an official consumer grievance channel for consumer complaints and related services.
Gold refinery licensing guidance BIS publishes official guidance for gold refineries, including scheme information, testing and marking requirements and licensed refinery resources.
Laboratory recognition information BIS publishes information and forms concerning recognition of laboratories for BIS product testing.
BIS guidelines BIS publishes official guidelines covering operational and technical subjects across its programmes.
Hallmarking consumer protection BIS provides consumer protection guidance covering testing of jewellery at BIS-recognized Assaying and Hallmarking Centres and assay reporting.

CRS registration process BIS CRS describes the registration workflow for products under the Compulsory Registration Scheme, including manufacturer registration, sample details, recognized laboratory testing, report verification and application.
CRS registration granularity BIS CRS guidance states that separate registration is required for each manufacturing location and for each brand where applicable under the scheme.
BIS-owned laboratory directory BIS LIMS publishes the current BIS laboratory directory. The LIMS home page currently reports 10 BIS laboratories.
CRS recognized-lab testing BIS CRS registration workflow includes testing through a BIS-recognized laboratory and verification of the test report before application processing.
BIS guideline source BIS maintains an official guidelines resource for operational and technical guidance.
Consumer publication source BIS publishes consumer-awareness and supporting material through official consumer engagement resources.
BIS Consumer Affairs BIS publishes consumer affairs information and services through its official Consumer Affairs section.
Hallmarking jeweller requirements BIS publishes official guidance for registered jewellers covering hallmarking, invoicing and consumer-facing requirements.
Consumer HUID verification BIS provides HUID verification through BIS Care and identifies consumer verification as an official hallmarking service.

BIS product certification licence process BIS explains that product certification begins by identifying the applicable Indian Standard and using product-specific manuals, assessment/testing requirements and the online application process.
Hallmarking FAQ collection BIS provides official hallmarking FAQ resources covering consumer, jeweller, assaying and hallmarking-centre questions.

Recognized laboratory directory fields BIS LIMS recognized-laboratory records expose laboratory code, laboratory name, address, contact person, contact number, email, validity date and a View Scope facility.
BIS empanelled laboratory directory BIS LIMS publishes the empanelled laboratory directory. The current LIMS home page reports 140 empanelled laboratories.

Hallmarked jewellery invoice information BIS Hallmarking FAQ guidance states that the invoice should include article description, net precious-metal weight, purity/caratage/fineness and hallmarking charges.
Jeweller responsibility BIS hallmarking jeweller guidance states that the registered jeweller is responsible for declared purity/fineness and related consumer-facing requirements.
Consumer awareness publications BIS publishes consumer-awareness material and supporting publications through its official consumer engagement resources.

Mandatory Hallmarking Order BIS publishes the Mandatory Hallmarking Order and associated amendments through its Hallmarking resources. The current BIS page lists amendments including updates through 3 August 2026.
BIS FAQ source BIS maintains an official FAQ resource covering questions across BIS programmes and services.
CRS registered manufacturer registry BIS CRS publishes a public registered manufacturer directory containing registration details and product/standard information.
AHC timing requirement BIS A&H Centre guidance contains requirements relating to processing and timing under the applicable A&H Centre standard and scheme documents.

Hallmarking FAQ: HUID and hallmark components BIS Hallmarking FAQ states that HUID is a six-digit alphanumeric unique identification number associated with a hallmarked item. The current hallmark comprises BIS logo, purity/caratage/fineness and HUID.

List of Hallmarking Centres BIS provides the official List of Hallmarking Centres through the Hallmarking Centre resource page. The BIS page identifies the list as an official resource and states it was last updated 31 July 2026.

Product Manual role BIS product certification FAQ explains that product manuals contain product-specific requirements such as sampling, equipment, Scheme of Inspection and Testing and scope-related information.
Current hallmark components BIS states that the hallmark includes the BIS logo, purity/caratage/fineness and the six-digit HUID.
BIS Care verification services BIS Care provides services including Verify Licence Details, Verify HUID, Know Your Standards, laboratory and office locations and scheme guidance.

Laboratory scope access BIS LIMS laboratory directory records provide a View Scope function for laboratory-specific scope information. Scope should be acquired as a separate authoritative record rather than inferred from laboratory names.
A&H Centre resource catalogue BIS provides A&H Centre guidelines, the official centre list, generic quality manual and lists of cancelled, expired and suspended A&H centres.
Hallmarking FAQ source BIS maintains a dedicated Hallmarking FAQ resource covering consumer, jeweller and A&H Centre questions.
Consumer grievance channel BIS maintains an official consumer grievance service for complaints and related consumer support.
